title: Implement the complete physical chirp Fourier consumer
body:
I complete source08's physical `Q_freq F_t` chirp consumer after [PR3709](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3709). I generate the numerical kernel from encoded residues and dyadic phase powers, execute both endpoint products, and run the complete twist/ring-convolution/exact-narrowing/untwist sequence in between.

For the declared p-grid contract, input norm at most .6 and p-A>=13, I return error below `(4sqrt(2)M+22)*2^-p` and norm below .601. I preserve the natural tensor order and borrowed ports, consume protected child returns and restore the fixed tape owners. I charge the phase and consumer work at `O(CT(ell+1)p^(8/5)+rp^3+(A+p+log(C+1))^3)`, in addition to three complete inherited Fourier calls. Under the stated outer hypotheses, the added power .603 fits the corrected full Fourier power .99827619697.

I build on Chafik Boukhalfa's [PR479](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/479) additive residue schedule and Ross Richardson's [PR948](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/948) symbolic checks. I add their encoded physical lowering, certified numerical phase evaluation and the whole consumer. I retain corrected PR3709 at `62264289adb01f3ba4930cd0154c75887f96203c`, its nested attribution and source07/source08 notices.

I started from canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6, and recorded the expansion gate and fresh overlap in [Discussion3664](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664). This PR changes only `research/physical-chirp-middle/`. [Arham Tahir's separate PR3709 audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664#discussioncomment-19022515) remains pending; I claim no acceptance result from it.

Validation at `6bb7dfdae182a69f7c8836a9ec1be0b2b747e124`:

- Seven registered suites passed locally, including the full p16 consumer against staged and dense exact Fourier models, 48 certified phase values, complete odometer cubes, a 40-axis prefix and 13 fault controls.
- I executed the full packet with the original reduced q2 setup and with an exact specialization of three certified metadata values. I obtained the same 288-bit payload. The registered specialization preserves the physical data, child, normalization and restoration execution; `EVIDENCE.md` explains its scope and exact certificates.
- Metadata, source-history and committed-byte checks passed. I replayed all seven commands outside Git on Darwin arm64, Python 3.12.13, and verified that all 30 regular files, including the receipt, remained unchanged. The complete middle-map check took 31.242 seconds.
- Official export SHA256: `e769b750eb650c4b2f7822a6e4780aa1b360c207ff9a724caa6dd2555ab3f54f`; receipt SHA256: `dca075b93c723087c167f01c1074031eeeed2d09d9eeb877481b735a0cecb495`. Hosted [CI39161347031](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39161347031) passed all seven suites and the unchanged-input check. I matched its merge tree to the published head tree `0533e11436d5036bfa04a616bf370947637156c6`.

Read `PROOF.md` and `EVIDENCE.md` for the argument and finite coverage. Reproduce with `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/physical-chirp-middle`.

I retain the inherited Fourier supplier/refinement premises. Production GL64/O73 execution and the Gaussian expansion/compression, CRT and final integer-recovery join remain open. I leave the selected frontier unchanged. Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including source-analysis agents; I claim no independent human review or formal-kernel verification.
